consumer.permission_owner: Generic ExecutionContext principals/grants/leases; no financial owner or per-payment approval bound in the observed code.
consumer.reason: Fixed-commit entry mediates generic capabilities, but this bounded official-source sample has no named, deployed money-transfer, merchant-charge, settlement or financial-signing consumer wired into that path. A marketplace extension could exist outside these samples; this result does not claim global nonexistence.

stages.name: entry
stages.reason: Only a general capability entry is statically proven: HostRuntime delegates to CapabilityHost and invokes generic workflows; no finance-specific effect can be attributed.

stages.name: prepared_object
stages.reason: No immutable financial transaction specification, owner-controlled prepared funds object, amount/payee provenance or fetch-by-spec-id execution input was demonstrated by fixed-version code. Issue #1712 is a design discussion, not code evidence.

stages.name: approval_authority
stages.reason: Generic approval resolver grants scoped capability leases and does not itself execute a tool; lease-issuance retry may mint a fresh grant ID, but no financial owner or per-transaction authorization has been observed.

stages.name: execution_consumption
stages.reason: The generic host documents invocation, authorization and dispatch but no pinned financial handler was traced through atomic spend authority consumption, original transaction identity and side-effect completion. Generic capability lease handling is not proof of exactly-once payment.

stages.name: credential_injection
stages.reason: HostWasmRuntimeCredentials stages scoped host-approved secret injection after provider account resolution and one-time secret lease; this static generic WASM path is not proof that any money tool uses it or that an external signing or PSP outcome occurred.

stages.name: outcome_recovery
stages.reason: A specific financial executor outcome, transaction query, failure/unknown state reconciliation, original-payment reuse and no-double-spend recovery were not shown in this pinned code sample. General approval suspension and lease issuance are different objects.

existing_coverage_comparison.subject: Prepared financial object / integrity
existing_coverage_comparison.reason: Local governed payment action has a representative object-binding model; pinned upstream financial persistent PaymentSpec consumer was not found, so no incremental implementation obligation was established.

existing_coverage_comparison.subject: Authorization intent / confirmation binding
existing_coverage_comparison.reason: Local confirmation and payment binding already represent approval-to-action checks; generic IronClaw capability approvals do not prove a new finance-specific consumer beyond those semantics.

existing_coverage_comparison.subject: Execution preflight and context trust
existing_coverage_comparison.reason: Local context policy and known-payment preflight already express fail-closed and retry/identity constraints; an additional concrete finance runtime bypass has not been observed.

existing_coverage_comparison.subject: Payment recovery and unknown status
existing_coverage_comparison.reason: Local recovery/original-transaction model has testable status distinctions; the generic IronClaw host does not show external PSP settlement or authoritative query recovery for a concrete payment.

existing_coverage_comparison.subject: Credential possession versus host injection
existing_coverage_comparison.reason: IronClaw documents generic WASM host credential staging, potentially a different external seam from local credential possession; without a money consumer there is no newly verifiable payment-control boundary.

existing_coverage_comparison.subject: Idempotency / replay of execution rights
existing_coverage_comparison.reason: ApprovalResolver notes fresh grant IDs on partial retry, while local controls already model replay risk; no trace linking duplicated leases to repeated funds execution is available, so this is not a proven duplicate-payment defect.

upstream_metadata.issue_1712: At observation time, closed; a financial read/prepare/spend design, not fixed-version runtime execution evidence.
upstream_metadata.issue_6532: At observation time, open; signing architecture proposal, not fixed-version completion evidence.

bounded_source_view.limitations: Only frozen official text files that were successfully archived and two permitted design issues. S07 blocked by local secret safety filter; S08 not-found path; S11/S12 connector-shape errors. No pinned tree nor exhaustive extension inventory. No PRs required to decide.

conclusion: The pinned IronClaw code demonstrates a generic capability host, scoped approval lease issuance, and host-controlled WASM credential injection; these are relevant reference designs but not a verified financial transaction consumer. A payment-specific prepared object, authority owner, fund-effect execution and transaction outcome recovery were not joined by code citations. Stop at REFERENCE_ONLY rather than adapt the runtime or invent a testable payment path.
